jobs.description:
For a description of key terms used on CRA job notices, go to Definitions for job seekers.

About The Job

The CRA is committed to providing an inclusive and barrier-free work environment with a diverse workforce that reflects the Canadians we serve. It starts with the hiring process. To find out more about the CRA's actions in support of Employment Equity (EE), diversity and inclusion (DI), and read testimonials from our employees and executives, please visit the following CRA web sites: Employment equity, diversity and inclusion and Our workforce testimonials - Canada.ca.

We encourage you to complete the EEDI Staffing questionnaire as part of your application if you wish to be considered for appointments using the EE and/or DI staffing requirement in this process. Also, ensure that you have provided consent in the EEDI staffing questionnaire for your EEDI information to be used for screening or selection. If you do not complete the questionnaire, you will not be considered for any appointments using the EE and/or DI staffing requirement in this process. If you decide to modify your response or fill out this questionnaire at a later date, please notify the contact listed at the bottom of this notice of job opportunity.

Have you ever wanted to make a difference to the lives of millions of people and influence how government interacts with Canadians? Are you inspired by the possibility of delivering results in a people-centric environment and in an organization that encourages innovation? Do you want to be part of a team that is engaged, collaborative and respectful?

If you answered yes to the above, THIS
is the job for you and CRA is THE
organization for you.

At the CRA, we recognize the importance of creating a healthy and respectful workplace, where our employees are empowered to be themselves and realize their full potential. We value integrity, respect, professionalism and collaboration. At the core of our values is our deep commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility. Through experience we know that diversity and inclusion foster innovation and leads to greater engagement, richer discussions, and better results for the people and communities we serve. Learn more about the CRA from an executive's perspective.

We are looking for dynamic, collaborative and strategic leaders with a proven track record to contribute to the People First vision and take the delivery of services to Canadians to the next level while demonstrating character leadership. The CRA is elevating character leadership alongside competencies, as "leading from who you are" is recognized as an important part of the CRA leadership practice.

The Intent Of This Staffing Process Is To Create a Pre-Qualified Pool (PQP) Of EX-02 Qualified Individuals With Specialized Expertise To Fill Current And Future Vacancies Within The Following Headquarters Branches:

Finance and Administration Branch (FAB) (Stream 1)
Information Technology Branch (ITB) (Stream 2)

Who Can Apply
:

Employees of the CRA who occupy a substantive position. If you are an eligible veteran or a Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) member, you may also apply.

For each stream, if the number of applicants is insufficient, the following may be considered: Persons who occupy a substantive position within the Federal Public Service, including Crown corporations and agencies.

Essential Requirements:

Education

For Stream 1 (FAB), have a degree (see note 1) from a recognized post-secondary institution.

For Steam 2 (ITB), have a degree (see note 1) or diploma in computer science, information technology, software/computer engineering, management information systems or a combination of career long IT experience and relevant education.

Experience

For both streams, have recent and significant experience
(see note 2) at the EX-01 group and level (or equivalent or above) in the following:

EXP1
:

Stream 1 (FAB):

Managing human and financial resources (Please be specific: indicate the number of direct reports, subordinates and the dollar figures of the budgets you directly managed for each position in the questionnaire); and

EXP2:

Providing strategic advice and briefings to senior officials (see note 3) on a large and complex (see note 4) program, major project (see note 5), policy or operational issues of a regional or national scale; and

EXP3:

Establishing and maintaining relationships with multiple internal or external stakeholders, which could include other government departments and agencies in order to deliver on government priorities; and

EXP4: (choose one of the following)

(4.1):
Leading, developing and implementing policies, programs, systems, or strategies related to Project and Portfolio Management in the financial field.

OR

(4.2):
Leading, developing and implementing policies, programs, systems, or strategies related to the finance functions such as (but not limited to): Resource Management and Budgeting, Accounting Operations, Financial Policy and Internal Controls, Financial Systems, Financial Reporting, Financial Management Administration, Costing, Internal Audit, Materiel Management or Procurement.

Stream 2 (ITB):

EXP1:

Managing significant human resources (40 FTEs or more) and financial resources ($5M or more); and

EXP2:

Leading complex (see note 4) and innovative services or solutions related to Information Management/ Information Technology (IM/IT) initiatives through subordinate supervisors in a large decentralized organization (see note 6) OR business transformation initiatives enabled by IT in a large decentralized organization; and

EXP3:

Collaborating and maintaining partnerships, and building consensus around issues with both colleagues and a variety of internal and external stakeholders; and

EXP4:

Experience in providing strategic advice and recommendations related to IT programs, major IT projects (see note 5) or IT-related issues to senior officials (see note 3).

This Experience Would Be Considered An Asset:

Steam 1 (FAB):

Providing leadership on corporate services, programs or operational service delivery.
Experience in leading a major complex and horizontal transformation initiative.
Possess or be eligible for a recognized professional accounting designation (CPA, including CA, CMA or CGA).
Experience interacting with central agencies; e.g., the Treasury Board Secretariat or the Department of Finance, on resource management matters.
Experience managing a major project investment or providing oversight of a portfolio of projects.

Stream 2 (ITB):

Broad and deep knowledge of current and emerging technologies (e.g. Artificial Intelligence, Cloud, Quantum), technology directions and strategic application of technologies to support business needs.
Experience in modern IT development practices and methodologies such as DevSecOps, decoupling applications through Application Programming Interfaces (API), Product Management and cloud.
Experience delivering excellent results (projects and operations) in a large complex environment with a mix of emerging, current and legacy technologies.
Experience in the planning, delivery and/or management of IT security programs, services or projects, including in cybersecurity.
Experience in leading more than one IT program (at the executive level) in a large scale organization (see note 6).
Experience providing leadership in information technology within a large organization responsible for the administration of tax and/or benefits programs.

Notes:

Degree: is defined as a baccalaureate or higher level degree.
Recent and significant experience is defined as the depth and breadth of the experience normally associated with having performed a broad range of related activities at the EX-01 group and level or equivalent and above, for a period of two (2) cumulative years in the past five (5) years.
Senior officials are defined as Director General, Assistant Commissioner/Deputy Assistant Commissioner (Assistant Deputy Minister) or equivalent and above.
Complex is defined as having at least three (3) of the following characteristics: multidimensional, sensitive, affecting many partners or stakeholders, precedent setting or having major impact on the organization, or having a potential for significant media coverage.
A major project would normally be an initiative under the oversight of the Agency's Major Project Investment Oversight Process (MPIOP), or other governmental organization equivalent.
A large decentralized organization is defined as a geographically decentralized organization with more than 5,000 employees whose operations are spread over a very large territory.

Conditions Of Employment Required At The Time Of Appointment:

Willingness to travel
Willingness to relocate to the National Capital Region (NCR)
For Steam 1 (FAB), candidates not currently located in NCR or within commuting distance must indicate in their application their willingness to relocate. Failure to do so at the time of application will result in being screened out of the staffing process.
For Stream 2 (ITB), relocate to the NCR may be required for some positions. Candidates not currently located in NCR or within commuting distance must indicate in their application their willingness to relocate. Failure to do so at the time of application may result in not being considered for some positions.

All appointments (except acting appointments) to and within the Executive (EX) Group at the CRA are subject to the Agreement to be laterally moved provision as a mandatory condition of employment. This provision is included in the CRA's Directive on Terms and Conditions of Employment for the EX Group

Languages Requirements:

Bilingual – CBC levels
Candidates must have valid Second Language Evaluation test results at the CBC level at the time of application in order to be considered further in the staffing process. Should your SLE results not be transferable to the CRA, you will be assessed and must meet to be considered further in this staffing process.

education;

name of organization;
duration (years and months); and
the number of direct and indirect reports, and the dollar figures of the budgets you directly managed and were accountable for.

jobs.title: Director of Solution Architecture
jobs.description:
At PwC Canada, we're transforming the way we work—and the way our people and clients experience technology. Our Products & Technology team builds the digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled platforms that power the firm and shape the future of professional services. We're a community of solvers combining technology, data, and human ingenuity to deliver sustained outcomes that matter. We're looking for a Director of Solution Architecture to lead our established team of Senior Solution Architects—a technically deep, business-savvy leader who can set direction, grow and develop talent, and partner with senior leaders across the firm to turn ambitious ideas into reality. Reporting to the Architecture and Development Leader, you will lead PwC Canada's Solution Architecture practice within Products & Technology. You will take ownership of our established team of Senior Solution Architects, elevate their performance, and grow the team's capabilities as our technology ambitions expand. The team designs AI-enabled products, enterprise applications, and platforms used across the firm's lines of service, ensuring our solutions are secure, scalable, resilient, aligned with enterprise architecture standards—and deliver real business value. This is a hands-on architecture leadership role. While your focus is on design and technical direction rather than execution, you'll be expected to understand the technology from the inside. You'll go deep into architecture diagrams, integration designs, data flows, platform configurations, and the realities of how solutions are implemented, engaging with technical trade-offs at a practitioner level. Your credibility with the team and with stakeholders will come from genuine technical depth and a willingness to go hands-on with architecture and implementation details when the situation calls for it, not from high-level concepts alone. Equally, this role operates at the intersection of business and technology. You'll be a trusted advisor to business stakeholders and organizational leaders, translating complex challenges into clear technology solutions, influencing strategic direction, and communicating in terms that resonate with executives. You'll also help shape how PwC Canada adopts emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI.

The Opportunity

As a Director of Solution Architecture, unlock your potential and embrace the chance to drive meaningful outcomes that’ll elevate your career. Your role will include, but isn’t limited to:

Provide architecture oversight for digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled solutions from ideation through production
Lead solution design decisions, balancing reusable platform components with business-specific needs
Guide the architecture of enterprise applications—including SaaS platforms, ERP, CRM, HR, finance, and collaboration systems—ensuring effective integration, extensibility, and alignment with our broader technology ecosystem
Go hands-on with architecture and technical implementation details when needed—working through complex integration patterns, data flows, platform configurations, or design problems alongside the team
Advise on the adoption of emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI
Manage, coach, and mentor an established team of talented Senior Solution Architects, elevating performance and fostering a culture of technical excellence and continuous learning
Grow the team's capabilities over time—identifying skill gaps, developing talent from within, and recruiting new members as the practice expands
Evolve team structure and define new roles as the practice grows and technology priorities shift
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Data, Security, and Risk teams to ensure solutions align with firm standards
Participate in architecture review boards and technology governance forums, advising on governance requirements, risk assessments, and policy exceptions
Contribute to PwC's broader architecture community—locally and across the global PwC network

What You’ll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here’s what we look for:

Experience in technology roles, including significant time in solution or enterprise architecture, with extensive experience designing and delivering solutions within large, complex organizations
Proven experience leading, developing, and growing a team of Senior Solution Architects—setting technical direction, elevating performance, and fostering a high-performance culture, including in an Agile/DevOps environment
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering
Azure Cloud Platform certifications (Solutions Architect or Developer) preferred; TOGAF certification
Strong technical depth as an architect—able to engage with the technology from the inside, work through implementation-level details, and go hands-on with architecture and design when the situation requires it
Enterprise application architecture, including SaaS and COTS platforms (ERP, CRM, HCM, finance, collaboration, workflow), integration patterns (APIs, iPaaS, event-driven), and configuration vs. customization trade-offs
Cloud-native architectures on Azure (AWS/GCP nice to have), including containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and DevOps practices such as CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code
Generative AI and agentic AI solution design, including LLM integration, RAG patterns, and responsible AI practices
Enterprise software architecture and design patterns, including service-oriented, event-driven, and microservices architectures; data architecture and persistence strategies (RDBMS, NoSQL); and Big Data, analytics, and AI/ML architecture
Security-by-design, privacy, and compliance considerations, plus vendor and product evaluation, including RFP processes, proof-of-concepts, and total-cost-of-ownership analysis
Demonstrated experience advising and partnering with senior business leaders on technology strategy and investment decisions; experience in professional services or consulting environments is an asset
This role does not require professional engineering licensure and is not classified as a formal engineering position under provincial regulatory definitions. While individuals with a P.Eng designation are welcome to apply, the responsibilities of this role do not involve the practice of professional engineering as defined by applicable legislation.

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.

The salary range for this position is $196,000 - $246,000. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc

PwC Canada acknowledges that we work and live across Turtle Island, on the land that is now known as Canada, which are the lands of the ancestral, treaty and unceded territories of the First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples. We recognize the systemic racism, colonialism and oppression that Indigenous Peoples have experienced and still go through, and we commit to allyship and solidarity.

We’re committed to providing accommodation throughout the application, interview, and employment process. If you require accommodation to be at your best, please let us know during the application process.

The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruiting is just getting started, so we know you have questions about how and why we use it. At certain points during our recruiting process, we rely on AI to improve your experience. This could be during resume review or curating personalized job recommendations, asking you clarifying questions via a chatbot or during our interview scheduling to improve your experience. Our use of AI helps ensure we combat bias by evaluating candidates equally and fairly, without seeing identity information, such as your name, or gender for example). AI also helps us better predict successful hires by reviewing all applicants for a role and the relationship between your skills, experience and likely success at PwC Canada. While AI supports parts of our recruitment process, final hiring decisions always involve human review. For more information about our use and protection of your data, please refer to our Privacy Policy (https://www.pwc.com/ca/en/privacy-policy.html).

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
About the role

Few Director roles hand you both finance and operations, and a mandate to rebuild them with AI tools. You get access to the engineering team for improvements implementation. This role has both, plus stock options, so you own a stake in the outcome.

Positrace is rebuilding how finance and operations run, and you lead it. You own the processes where the two meet, across Canada and Mexico, and you lead an AI-first transformation and tool automation across operations and finance processes.

This is a builder's seat. You get an engineering team that ships what you specify, an in-house data and AI platform, and executives who want the change. If you have transformed a process end to end and want a first Director role with real scope, this is it.

You report to the COO , with a dotted line to the CFO for finance, and have direct access to CEO.

What you will own

Hands-on first
You run every core process yourself a few times before you change, delegate or automate it. You will know the business from the inside, and your notes become the procedure and the automation spec.

Finance
Month-end close and controls.
Own/supervise close for three entities to a calendar, reduce time to close.
Tax and compliance calendar.
One calendar for Canada and Mexico, and nothing filed late.
Billing and collections.
Invoices that tie to the ledger and payments that apply themselves.
Cash and treasury operations.
Instrumented and automated, starting with a 13-week forecast that refreshes itself.
Reporting and planning automation.
Designed with the CFO, so the management pack assembles itself from the ledgers.
Audit readiness.
Audit-ready by fiscal 2027 year end.

Operations
Procurement and suppliers.
Vendor management and forecasting for hardware and connectivity in two countries.
Quote approval and deal margin automation.
You set the margin and payback rules; the system checks every quote.
Inventory, warehouse and logistics reporting.
Two warehouses, and stock that matches the count.
Procedures and governance.
Every process written down, owned and followed.
Operating cost management and control.
Spend that ties to the ledgers, and savings you can show.

Systems and automation
Billing platform.
You are the business process owner. Engineering builds; you set the rules and sign off every change.
AI automation.
Built with the CTO's team on Cortex, our in-house AI platform. Finance first, then operations.
Ledger and ERP path.
Yours to recommend: build our platform into an accounting-grade subledger, or move to a full ERP.
One system of record per process.
No parallel spreadsheets.

Team
You lead the operations team and the finance teams in both countries. The Controller reports to you. Automate first, hire second.
You work alongside the CFO, who leads lenders, the board, tax strategy and accounting policy. You prepare, the CFO reviews and signs, and you learn the capital side from the seat next to it.

Who you are

Must have

At least 5 years in audit at a Big 4 or national firm, and a CPA designation. We see audit as the school.
At least 2 years of hands-on finance work in industry, at a software or hardware company. This is where you learned to manage and to deliver change fast.
Multi-subsidiary experience: you have closed and consolidated across entities.
Finance experience at a company with at least CAD 20 million in revenue, where automation is a necessity.
One transformation you led from start to finish, with a before and an after to show.
You build with tools yourself: AI scripting, workflow automation.
You have managed people and are ready to lead managers.
You document what you own, so others can run it without you.
Based in Metro Vancouver, or relocating, working from our Burnaby office and able to travel to our Mexico office.

Good to have

A recurring-revenue business model, ideally one that also ships hardware.
Cross-border, multi-currency accounting, especially Canada and Mexico.
Spanish is a nice to have, but AI translation will help you otherwise.
Procurement, inventory or field-operations exposure.

This is likely your first Director role. We care more about what you have changed, and how fast your scope has grown, than about the size of your last title. If you have the first five and the drive, we want to hear from you.

What we offer

Finance and operations in one seat.
Breadth that most Director roles do not offer.
Stock options.
You share in the value you help build.
Room to build.
An engineering team, an in-house data and AI platform, and leaders who want the old way replaced.
A seat at the table.
You sit on the senior leadership team and work directly with the CEO.
Scope that grows as you deliver.
You take on the role in phases, and each one you land opens the next.
Salary range:
CAD $150,000 to $180,000 per year, plus stock options and benefits.
Location:
Burnaby, BC (Metrotown). You work from our Burnaby office and travel to our Mexico office in Guadalajara as needed.

About Positrace and how to apply

Positrace builds fleet management software: GPS telematics, connected cameras and asset tracking for commercial fleets in Canada and Mexico. We have been in business for 19 years, and thousands of vehicle fleets trust Positrace every day. We are founder-led and profitable, with teams in Burnaby and Guadalajara.

To apply, send your résumé and a short note, one page at most, describing one process you transformed: what it was, what you changed, and the measured result.

Positrace is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates.

jobs.description:
Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Director, People Platform & Self-Service Experience

Reporting to the Senior Director, People Experience (PE) Technology Systems, you will own the end-to-end experience across People Experience products and services. You will partner across PE, IT, and the user community to develop a vision and prioritized roadmap for opportunities to create PE technology experiences that meet EA employees where they are. One of your major initial focuses will be on establishing the experiences that integrate EA's new PE AI Assistant.

This is not a traditional HR operations or technology role. We are looking for someone who thinks like a product and service designer: You are curious about users, able to simplify complex systems, and are comfortable working across technology, process and organizational boundaries. You will work in a hybrid work model 3 days in office based in out of Los Angeles, CA, Kirkland, WA, or Vancouver, Canada
.

Responsibilities

End-to-end ownership of PE digital experiences

Define the PE digital experience strategy that will transform how employees and managers interact with digital PE products and services.
Design experiences around what employees and managers are trying to accomplish rather than around PE's internal organizational structure.
Launch the manager and employee experience product roadmaps.

Integrate AI Into PE Digital Experiences

Establish the vision for how PE can unify AI experiences across disparate EA core and PE platforms (Workday, Google Gemini, and others) into a uniform experience.
Lead the user experience design for the PE AI Assistant (AIA), from initial launch through continued expansion.
Define and drive implementation of digital journeys that optimize the use and adoption of the AI-enabled digital experiences.
Use interaction data and user feedback to continuously improve PE's digital products.

Launch & Own Manager and Employee Experience Products & Journeys

Lead the end-to-end design, launch, and ongoing management of core manager and employee experience products and journeys.
Partner with PE teams to redesign priority journeys across the talent lifecycle to bring together policy, process, technology, data and service delivery into satisfying user experiences.
Establish and track product success metrics, defining how we measure PE experience quality through measures such as employee effort, task completion, adoption, AI resolution, human handoffs, and satisfaction.
Use data from the AIA, People Services, technology platforms, and direct user feedback to identify improvement opportunities and create a continuous feedback loop into PE's product and process roadmap.

Build User-Centered Design Into How PE Works

Establish practical approaches for user research, prototyping and testing across PE.
Bring employees and managers into the design process early and regularly.
Partner with transformation teams and workstream leads to embed experience design into design sprints.
Create reusable design patterns and standards that allow teams to move quickly while maintaining a consistent experience.
Act as the voice of the user in major PE product, process and technology decisions.

Required Qualifications

7+ years of experience in service design, UX, product management, or customer or employee experience in a global enterprise.
Experience designing end-to-end user journeys across digital products, operational processes, and service delivery.
Experience integrating AI capabilities to improve the efficacy and quality of employee or customer experiences

Core Skills And Experience

If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.

Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.

10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.

Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.

At Gore Mutual, we’ve always set ourselves apart as a modern mutual that does good. Now, we’re proudly building on that legacy to transform our company—and our industry—for the better.
Effective January 1, 2026, Gore has joined Beneva—the country’s largest mutual insurance company—as part of its Property & Casualty operations in Ontario and Western Canada. During 2026, Gore will combine its operations with Unica Insurance, Beneva’s Ontario-based subsidiary specializing in niche commercial and personal insurance, creating a stronger, more diversified mutual insurer with greater scale and long-term stability.
Every decision and investment remains anchored in long-term benefits to customers, members, and communities. Come join us.
We are looking for a Director, Data Engineering to lead a critical capability within Gore’s Enterprise Data & Analytics organization. You will lead the teams responsible for turning enterprise data into trusted, reusable data products and building the engineering capabilities that enable Data, Insights and AI across Gore.
You will shape how we build and manage data products, evolve our Data Engineering and MLOps capabilities, and ensure our Databricks and Azure ecosystem provides the foundation needed for Analytics, Data Science, GenAI and emerging AI solutions.
This is a visible leadership role for someone who combines strong technical depth with business understanding, people leadership and the ability to turn data and technology investments into meaningful business outcomes.
What will you do?

Build Enterprise Data Products

Lead the development of trusted, reusable data products that combine business meaning, data quality and strong engineering to support operational, analytical, Data Science and AI use cases.
Establish and mature our data product discipline, partnering with business and technology leaders to turn high-value data needs into scalable capabilities.
Improve the accessibility, consistency and value of enterprise data while reducing fragmentation and duplication.

Advance Data Engineering & AI Enablement

Lead and mature Data Engineering and MLOps capabilities, creating repeatable paths to move data, machine learning, GenAI and emerging AI solutions into secure, reliable production.
Raise engineering standards across integration, APIs, orchestration, CI/CD, testing, observability, automation, data quality and production operations.
Partner across Data, Analytics and technology teams to provide the engineering capabilities needed to scale Data Science and AI.

Evolve Our Data Technology Foundation

Guide the evolution of Gore’s Databricks and Azure ecosystem to provide a scalable, resilient, secure and cost-effective foundation for Data, Insights and AI.
Partner with IT and Architecture to shape architecture patterns, integration approaches and technology standards.
Evaluate emerging Data and AI technologies based on business value, scalability, security and long-term sustainability.

Build and Lead a Strong Engineering Organization

Lead, coach and develop high-performing teams across Data Products, Data Platforms, Data Engineering and MLOps.
Develop strong managers and technical leaders with clear accountability for products, engineering quality and production outcomes.
Build a culture of ownership, curiosity, continuous improvement and engineering excellence.

Provide Visible Enterprise Leadership

Represent Data Engineering with senior business and technology leaders, vendors and strategic partners.
Translate complex technology decisions into clear business implications, trade-offs, risks and recommendations.
Provide clear leadership across priorities, investments, delivery and significant operational challenges.

What will you need to succeed?

A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
Significant leadership experience across Data Engineering, data products, data platforms, MLOps or related enterprise technology functions.
Proven experience building enterprise data products and translating business needs into reusable, scalable data capabilities.
Proven experience building and operating enterprise-scale data platforms and production data workloads.
Direct production experience with Databricks, including data engineering, lakehouse architecture, governance and optimization.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure and modern cloud data architectures.
Strong technical knowledge of Python, SQL, APIs, data integration, orchestration and distributed processing.
Experience with technologies such as Delta Lake, Unity Catalog and MLflow, or comparable capabilities.
Experience with CI/CD, automated testing, observability, DevOps, DataOps and modern production engineering practices.
Practical MLOps experience enabling Data Science, machine learning and AI workloads in production.
Experience enabling GenAI or emerging AI capabilities in secure enterprise environments.
A strong track record of coaching and developing engineers, managers and technical leaders.
Strong executive presence and the ability to influence senior business, technology and external stakeholders.

The CRA is committed to providing an inclusive and barrier-free work environment with a diverse workforce that reflects the Canadians we serve. It starts with the hiring process. Information Technology Branch (ITB) (Stream 2)

:

Employees of the CRA who occupy a substantive position. If you are an eligible veteran or a Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) member, you may also apply.

For each stream, if the number of applicants is insufficient, the following may be considered: Persons who occupy a substantive position within the Federal Public Service, including Crown corporations and agencies.

For Steam 2 (ITB), have a degree (see note 1) or diploma in computer science, information technology, software/computer engineering, management information systems or a combination of career long IT experience and relevant education.

(see note 2) at the EX-01 group and level (or equivalent or above) in the following:

:

Leading, developing and implementing policies, programs, systems, or strategies related to the finance functions such as (but not limited to): Resource Management and Budgeting, Accounting Operations, Financial Policy and Internal Controls, Financial Systems, Financial Reporting, Financial Management Administration, Costing, Internal Audit, Materiel Management or Procurement.

Stream 2 (ITB):

EXP1:

Managing significant human resources (40 FTEs or more) and financial resources ($5M or more); and

EXP2:

Leading complex (see note 4) and innovative services or solutions related to Information Management/ Information Technology (IM/IT) initiatives through subordinate supervisors in a large decentralized organization (see note 6) OR business transformation initiatives enabled by IT in a large decentralized organization; and

EXP3:

Collaborating and maintaining partnerships, and building consensus around issues with both colleagues and a variety of internal and external stakeholders; and

EXP4:

Experience in providing strategic advice and recommendations related to IT programs, major IT projects (see note 5) or IT-related issues to senior officials (see note 3).

This Experience Would Be Considered An Asset:

Steam 1 (FAB):

Providing leadership on corporate services, programs or operational service delivery.
Experience in leading a major complex and horizontal transformation initiative.
Possess or be eligible for a recognized professional accounting designation (CPA, including CA, CMA or CGA).
Experience interacting with central agencies; e.g., the Treasury Board Secretariat or the Department of Finance, on resource management matters.
Experience managing a major project investment or providing oversight of a portfolio of projects.

Stream 2 (ITB):

Broad and deep knowledge of current and emerging technologies (e.g. Artificial Intelligence, Cloud, Quantum), technology directions and strategic application of technologies to support business needs.
Experience in modern IT development practices and methodologies such as DevSecOps, decoupling applications through Application Programming Interfaces (API), Product Management and cloud.

Experience in the planning, delivery and/or management of IT security programs, services or projects, including in cybersecurity.
Experience in leading more than one IT program (at the executive level) in a large scale organization (see note 6).
Experience providing leadership in information technology within a large organization responsible for the administration of tax and/or benefits programs.

Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Director, People Platform & Self-Service Experience

Reporting to the Senior Director, People Experience (PE) Technology Systems, you will own the end-to-end experience across People Experience products and services. You will partner across PE, IT, and the user community to develop a vision and prioritized roadmap for opportunities to create PE technology experiences that meet EA employees where they are. One of your major initial focuses will be on establishing the experiences that integrate EA's new PE AI Assistant.

This is not a traditional HR operations or technology role. We are looking for someone who thinks like a product and service designer: You are curious about users, able to simplify complex systems, and are comfortable working across technology, process and organizational boundaries. You will work in a hybrid work model 3 days in office based in out of Los Angeles, CA, Kirkland, WA, or Vancouver, Canada
.

Responsibilities

End-to-end ownership of PE digital experiences

Define the PE digital experience strategy that will transform how employees and managers interact with digital PE products and services.
Design experiences around what employees and managers are trying to accomplish rather than around PE's internal organizational structure.
Launch the manager and employee experience product roadmaps.

Integrate AI Into PE Digital Experiences

Establish the vision for how PE can unify AI experiences across disparate EA core and PE platforms (Workday, Google Gemini, and others) into a uniform experience.
Lead the user experience design for the PE AI Assistant (AIA), from initial launch through continued expansion.
Define and drive implementation of digital journeys that optimize the use and adoption of the AI-enabled digital experiences.
Use interaction data and user feedback to continuously improve PE's digital products.

Launch & Own Manager and Employee Experience Products & Journeys

Lead the end-to-end design, launch, and ongoing management of core manager and employee experience products and journeys.
Partner with PE teams to redesign priority journeys across the talent lifecycle to bring together policy, process, technology, data and service delivery into satisfying user experiences.
Establish and track product success metrics, defining how we measure PE experience quality through measures such as employee effort, task completion, adoption, AI resolution, human handoffs, and satisfaction.
Use data from the AIA, People Services, technology platforms, and direct user feedback to identify improvement opportunities and create a continuous feedback loop into PE's product and process roadmap.

Build User-Centered Design Into How PE Works

Establish practical approaches for user research, prototyping and testing across PE.
Bring employees and managers into the design process early and regularly.
Partner with transformation teams and workstream leads to embed experience design into design sprints.
Create reusable design patterns and standards that allow teams to move quickly while maintaining a consistent experience.

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership

Problem solving

Results orientation and a bias for action

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

new_jobs.description:
At Gore Mutual, we’ve always set ourselves apart as a modern mutual that does good. Now, we’re proudly building on that legacy to transform our company—and our industry—for the better.
Effective January 1, 2026, Gore has joined Beneva—the country’s largest mutual insurance company—as part of its Property & Casualty operations in Ontario and Western Canada. During 2026, Gore will combine its operations with Unica Insurance, Beneva’s Ontario-based subsidiary specializing in niche commercial and personal insurance, creating a stronger, more diversified mutual insurer with greater scale and long-term stability.
Every decision and investment remains anchored in long-term benefits to customers, members, and communities. Come join us.
We are looking for a Director, Data Engineering to lead a critical capability within Gore’s Enterprise Data & Analytics organization. You will lead the teams responsible for turning enterprise data into trusted, reusable data products and building the engineering capabilities that enable Data, Insights and AI across Gore.
You will shape how we build and manage data products, evolve our Data Engineering and MLOps capabilities, and ensure our Databricks and Azure ecosystem provides the foundation needed for Analytics, Data Science, GenAI and emerging AI solutions.
This is a visible leadership role for someone who combines strong technical depth with business understanding, people leadership and the ability to turn data and technology investments into meaningful business outcomes.
What will you do?

Build Enterprise Data Products

Lead the development of trusted, reusable data products that combine business meaning, data quality and strong engineering to support operational, analytical, Data Science and AI use cases.
Establish and mature our data product discipline, partnering with business and technology leaders to turn high-value data needs into scalable capabilities.
Improve the accessibility, consistency and value of enterprise data while reducing fragmentation and duplication.

Advance Data Engineering & AI Enablement

Lead and mature Data Engineering and MLOps capabilities, creating repeatable paths to move data, machine learning, GenAI and emerging AI solutions into secure, reliable production.
Raise engineering standards across integration, APIs, orchestration, CI/CD, testing, observability, automation, data quality and production operations.
Partner across Data, Analytics and technology teams to provide the engineering capabilities needed to scale Data Science and AI.

Evolve Our Data Technology Foundation

Guide the evolution of Gore’s Databricks and Azure ecosystem to provide a scalable, resilient, secure and cost-effective foundation for Data, Insights and AI.
Partner with IT and Architecture to shape architecture patterns, integration approaches and technology standards.
Evaluate emerging Data and AI technologies based on business value, scalability, security and long-term sustainability.

Build and Lead a Strong Engineering Organization

Lead, coach and develop high-performing teams across Data Products, Data Platforms, Data Engineering and MLOps.
Develop strong managers and technical leaders with clear accountability for products, engineering quality and production outcomes.
Build a culture of ownership, curiosity, continuous improvement and engineering excellence.

Provide Visible Enterprise Leadership

Represent Data Engineering with senior business and technology leaders, vendors and strategic partners.
Translate complex technology decisions into clear business implications, trade-offs, risks and recommendations.
Provide clear leadership across priorities, investments, delivery and significant operational challenges.

What will you need to succeed?

A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
Significant leadership experience across Data Engineering, data products, data platforms, MLOps or related enterprise technology functions.
Proven experience building enterprise data products and translating business needs into reusable, scalable data capabilities.
Proven experience building and operating enterprise-scale data platforms and production data workloads.
Direct production experience with Databricks, including data engineering, lakehouse architecture, governance and optimization.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure and modern cloud data architectures.
Strong technical knowledge of Python, SQL, APIs, data integration, orchestration and distributed processing.
Experience with technologies such as Delta Lake, Unity Catalog and MLflow, or comparable capabilities.
Experience with CI/CD, automated testing, observability, DevOps, DataOps and modern production engineering practices.
Practical MLOps experience enabling Data Science, machine learning and AI workloads in production.
Experience enabling GenAI or emerging AI capabilities in secure enterprise environments.
A strong track record of coaching and developing engineers, managers and technical leaders.
Strong executive presence and the ability to influence senior business, technology and external stakeholders.

This posting pertains to an existing vacancy that is actively being filled.

If you require accommodation because of a disability, we will work with you to meet your needs. Contact us and a human resources representative will consult with you to determine an appropriate accommodation.
